cases.name: Anna Marie List
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Anna spent most of her life in Ann Arbor and attended Angell Elementary and Tappan Middle schools. At the time of her death, Anna was a senior at Huron High School and was scheduled to graduate with her classmates this coming June. Anna was a talented musician and began playing violin at age seven and piano at age eight. She was a member of the Huron High School Orchestra and received many solo and ensemble competition awards Anna was a gifted artist as well as a staff member of Huron High School's Full Circle literary magazine. She was head coordinator of the Scarlett Middle School Strings Mentoring Program for young orchestra students and a member of Interact, a Rotary-sponsored volunteering organization. Anna had wanted to be a mentor for Washtenaw Literacy and briefly considered sneaking into the mentoring program but resolved not to as she did not yet meet the age requirement. Anna had several choices of colleges for this September, but she had not yet decided on which one to attend. She touched, changed and saved many lives through donation of her organs to the Gift of Life."
cases.narrative: She died on 1/19/2009. After an argument in a van, Oyerinde smacked her in the back of the head with a hammer as they were walking, then struck her again on the forehead as she fell in the snow in a nearby park. The senior at Ann Arbor's Huron High School died a week later at a local hospital, never regaining consciousness.

cases.name: Andrea Marie Grant
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Andrea was an amazing mom, and was the definition of dedication and love. She loved, cared for, guided, consoled, pushed, and rooted for her girls every single day. She was so full of pride as Mackenzie passed her boards and when Hannah became the leader and captain of her volleyball team. Both of Andrea’s girls love their mom with everything they have and always will.

Everyone who knew Andrea described her as amazing, and her list of accomplishments show it. Whether it was being selected as homecoming queen, earning a softball scholarship, being a director of a ‘Fortune 100’ company, or getting a new company up and off the ground - Andrea was a rockstar.  She was one of a kind that could juggle two laptops, three phones, a volleyball schedule, family functions, and workout regimen all while making time to keep in touch with all she loved and supported.

As a business owner, Andrea was an amazing innovator and completely dedicated to her team.  Even as she faced the toughest personal and professional challenges, her first priority was always the well-being of her people.  So many people looked up to Andrea and worked hard to mentor and help bring other people with her as she elevated to a whole new level.

Andrea will be best known for loving her children, her family, and friends and how she filled her home with warmth and kindness. She always put others before herself and provided comfort and solace to them and to anyone in need while asking for nothing in return.  Her family appreciates anyone who may wish to send notes with memories or photos of their times with her describing how she positively touched their life.

Andrea’s life was too short.  To say that her family and friends will miss her greatly is an understatement, but to those who were blessed to be touched by her understand that her time on this earth and the imprint she left on their hearts greatly exceed the quantity of time that she had with us. She was a beloved mother, daughter, sister, aunt, niece, and friend to many.  Her beautiful, kind spirit will be missed by all who knew and loved her.

We wish her celebration of life to be full of vibrancy and joy because that is how she lived her life."

cases.name: Judith Anne "Jude" Walton
cases.about:
Jude was a community activist who was described as a remarkable person. "She touched a lot of people’s lives here, she was such a fantastic person," said Peter Smith. "She just accepted you for who you were, she was kind, generous," said Catherine Christmas. She was also a former police oversight commissioner.

Her obituary said, "She was a beloved friend, community leader, business partner, colleague, and cat mom. Jude was born on March 6, 1972 in Ilford, Essex, the child of Peter Walton and Sandra Elizabeth Walton, and grew up in North London where her family moved shortly afterwards. She graduated with a BA from Jesus College Cambridge University where she studied English. After graduating Jude came to live in Ann Arbor, Michigan. She co-founded Zingermans Mail Order in 1995 and was a managing partner in the Zingerman's Community of Businesses for the next 13 years. In 2008, Jude joined Avalon Housing, a non-profit that works to end homelessness by developing affordable housing centered on community, care and support. She led the Employee Experience team until her passing. Jude was someone everyone went to for advice, encouragement, or a shoulder to cry on. She was a culture-bearer wherever she worked. She was a great friend, a wonderful listener and cared passionately about her community and world. Jude was an avid photographer. She exhibited locally and employed her talents to capture important moments in the lives of her friends and coworkers."
cases.narrative: On 4/13/2023, she was found dead after Ann Arbor police were called to do a well-being check at her home where there was evidence of a break-in, according to police. She died of strangulation. Investigators say her killer broke a window to get inside. She had ligature marks on her neck and bruising on her inner thighs.
